minutes.headline: Selectmen backed state bond-bill priorities, set the economic development charge and added a liquor change fee
minutes.summary: The board heard a selectman announce his resignation and took public comment. It held appointments on a Salvation Army boot drive, a restaurant name change and a skate park update, plus a hearing on license fees. It discussed FY20 budget priorities and special town meeting preparation, and voted on bond bill priorities, the economic development charge, two policies and the Gilchrist Street land.

what_happened.line: The board adopted its bond bill priorities and adopted the charge for the economic development committee.
The board set a Sunday entertainment license fee and a change fee for liquor licenses after a public hearing.
The board voted to convey the 161 Gilchrist Street property and to acquire part of 171 Gilchrist Street with a conservation restriction.
The chair will hold off signing the Gilchrist Street documents until the Conservation Commission reviews them.
The board adopted amendments to the investment policy and the appointment policy.

why_it_matters: The new license fees fall on local restaurants and liquor license holders, and the Gilchrist Street votes change what land the town owns and how it may be used.
The bond bill priorities, the economic development charge and the FY20 budget discussion shape which projects and spending the town pursues and how much of it falls on the tax bill.
watch_next: The November 13 special town meeting, where residents vote on the warrant articles, including article 17 on plastic bags.
The Conservation Commission review of the Gilchrist Street documents, which must happen before the chair signs.
